name: Erin Gerstenzang
tagline: Top rated Criminal Defense attorney in Atlanta, Georgia
about: I defend people when everything is on the line—their freedom, their license, their livelihood, their reputation.

As founding partner of EHG Law Firm, a boutique criminal defense practice at Ponce City Market in Atlanta, I've built a firm around one core belief: serious cases deserve serious lawyering . We handle high-stakes DUI, traffic, and criminal matters with the kind of meticulous preparation and strategic thinking that can make all the difference when it matters most.

What sets us apart isn't just our track record—it's how much we care. Every client gets our full attention, our best thinking, and our relentless advocacy. We dig into the details that others overlook: investigative procedures, evidentiary gaps, constitutional protections, the science behind the prosecution's case. We prepare every case like it's going to trial, because that preparation is what creates leverage, protects rights, and produces results.

Beyond the courtroom, I'm deeply invested in elevating the practice of criminal defense. I teach trial advocacy, legal ethics, and technology to lawyers across the country. I serve as President of the Georgia Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers and Vice Chair of the State Bar's Disciplinary Rules and Procedures Committee. I've been honored as an ABA Women in Legal Tech honoree, a Fastcase 50 recipient, and recipient of GAWL's Visionary Award and GACDL's President's Award. Law.com named me Best Mentor.
But the work that matters most happens one case, one client at a time—bringing skill, judgment, and genuine care to people facing the most difficult moments of their lives.

Honoring the law’s smartest, most courageous innovators, techies, visionaries, & leaders. Lawyer or nonlawyer, techie or non techie, anyone is eligible. Created in 2011, each year the Fastcase 50 award honors a diverse group of lawyers, legal technologists, policymakers, judges, law librarians, bar association executives, and people from all walks of life. In many cases, honorees are well known, but in many others, the award recognizes people who have made important, but unheralded contributions. “Every part of the legal market is changing right now – from law school through every part of the practice,” said Fastcase CEO Ed Walters. “That change can be daunting or discouraging to many people. And that’s one reason that our team enjoys celebrating the accomplishments of the Fastcase 50. These are people who inspire us by their intelligence, creativity, and leadership. We hope they will inspire others as well, especially during a time of great change for the profession.” , Fastcase 50 , Fastcase , 2018
